content.title: Browse the /publish package list with available, one-seat-left, and fully booked packages
content.intent: Prove the package comparison page shows the fixed package set, package-card features, seat-capacity messaging, and the correct action for packages with plural remaining seats, exactly one remaining seat, and no seats left.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: eqp for package and availability-state classes; bva for seat-count boundaries. expand_bva on bounds min=1 and max=6 returned authoritative variants 0, 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, which justified exercising the outcome-changing boundaries at 1 remaining seat and 0 remaining seats plus the plural class above 1. Risk-judged interaction strength was 3 because money applies, but no covering-array reduction was used here because the outcome changes by availability class, so those classes stayed explicit within one boundary journey. Budget ceiling 3 applied; this scenario was retained as highest value because it covers the shared-seat behavior that changes package choice across all visitors.

content.title: Open each publishing package detail page and verify commercial details
content.intent: Prove every real package detail page exposes its package code, tagline, price, turnaround in business days, and feature list.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: eqp across the four real package identities; covering_array requested at strength 3 because money applies and degraded to effective strength 1 because there is only one input dimension (package). The authoritative package coverage set enumerated Starter, Standard, Premium, and Author's Choice, so this one happy-path scenario sweeps all four as equivalent-input variations without splitting them into separate outcome paths. Budget ceiling 3 applied; this scenario was retained because it covers the published package facts authors compare before purchase.

content.title: Request a publishing package that does not exist and receive a 404 page
content.intent: Prove an invalid package request returns a 404 response instead of a generic error page.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: negative for the missing-resource path; eqp between existing package requests and nonexistent package requests, with the nonexistent class separated because it changes the outcome from a detail view to a 404. Budget ceiling 3 applied; this scenario was retained because the source promised a distinct failure mode that protects the package-discovery flow from generic errors.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Highest value because it covers the money-facing package-selection state changes at plural seats, singular seat, and fully booked capacity, plus the globally shared seat-pool rule that affects every author.
[value_score] High value because it verifies the published commercial facts on the detail pages for every legitimate package, which authors use to compare paid options.
[value_score] Moderate value because it covers the promised negative path for bad package requests and guards against a generic error page, but it affects fewer users than the main comparison flows.
